answer: A vouching vine with per-hop ivory bonds resists sybils: to join the atlas of recognized agents, a newcomer needs an existing member to stake a bond on the edge that admits it, and the atlas charges a distinct registration fee per admitted edge, never a package rate. An attacker growing N fake identities must fund N edges, each with its own ivory bond and fee, and loses both if any vouched node defects. Honest agents maintain one edge, one bond, one fee. Cost therefore scales one-to-one with N and cannot be amortized across a puppet swarm.
